notes: Deal choice. Trust names and CIKs come from the EDGAR quarterly ABS-EE index lists for 2026 Q3/Q4 saved earlier in Veritas_Hackathon_2026_Finance_Ideas/feature_hunt/lanes/3_data/sec/, which list Nissan Auto Receivables trusts 2022-B, 2023-A, 2023-B, 2024-A, 2024-B, 2025-A, 2025-B, 2026-A and 2026-B; filing dates come from each trust's data.sec.gov submissions JSON. Brief windows: Jan-Jun 2024 -> 2024-A (pool ABS-EE 2024-05-07); Jan-Jun 2025 -> 2025-A (2025-05-13, amended 2025-05-16); Oct 2025-Feb 28 2026 -> 2025-B (2025-11-07, large pool refiled 2025-11-19), the latest Nissan pool filing in that window: the next trust, 2026-A, first filed 2026-05-11. All three are Nissan Auto Receivables Owner Trusts (prime retail loans; Nissan's lease trusts file under Nissan Auto Leasing LLC II and were not used).

Pool files. Nissan files one pool ABS-EE per deal size before the 424B5: 'sp' and 'lp' (2024-A, 2025-B), 'sp', 'mp' and 'lp' (2025-A). In all three deals the 'lp' file's row count equals the 424B5 'Number of Receivables' exactly (66,593; 64,964; 52,533). 2025-A: the 2025-05-13 files were replaced on 2025-05-16/19 by ABS-EE/A filings; the lp amendment's cover page says it adds payment-to-income values inadvertently omitted and supersedes the original Exhibit 102 in its entirety, so the amended lp file (filing_date 2025-05-16) is the one parsed. 2025-B: the lp pool was filed on 2025-11-07 and again on 2025-11-19, both for the same $1,381,270,659.94 pool; a loan-by-loan comparison found the same 52,533 asset numbers and one difference, 12 payment-to-income values missing in the earlier file, so the 2025-11-19 file is parsed. Each parsed file's size equals the size in EDGAR's index.json.

Cutoff balance check. In all three deals the sum of reportingPeriodActualEndBalanceAmount equals the 424B5 Aggregate Principal Balance to the cent ($1,424,116,746.73; $1,668,465,701.04; $1,381,270,659.94). Weighted by it, the file reproduces the 424B5 summary: weighted APR 4.8087% / 4.4630% / 4.6017% (424B5 4.81% / 4.46% / 4.60%), weighted credit score 780.97 / 789.83 / 795.05 (424B5 'Non-Zero Weighted Average Credit Score' 781 / 790 / 795), share of new_used_code '1' 89.52% / 93.03% / 90.02% (424B5 'New' 89.52% / 93.03% / 90.02%).

new_used_code '2' is Nissan's 'Near-New' class: the 424B5 splits the pool into New, Near-New (10.48% / 6.97% / 9.98% of balance) and Used (0.00% in all three), and the code-2 balance share equals the Near-New share. So in these pools '2' means near-new, not an ordinary used car.

pti_pct differs from CONTRACT's formula on purpose: Nissan writes paymentToIncomePercentage in percent (median 6.95 / 7.11 / 6.79, e.g. 7.45 = 7.45%), while CarMax and Toyota write a fraction (0.0745). Multiplying by 100 would give 695%, so pti_pct is the file value as written. The value 999.99 appears in 6 / 3 / 6 rows (kept; looks like a placeholder, not confirmed); pti_pct is missing (NaN) in 2 / 1,356 / 0 rows (2025-A's amendment still leaves 1,356 blank).

Credit scores: obligorCreditScoreType is 'FICO' for every loan and every score is numeric (100%). Range 660-900 in all three deals, equal to the 424B5 'Range of FICO Scores 660 to 900'; medians 786 / 794 / 797. Scores above 850 (9,087 / 10,266 / 8,465 rows) fit the auto-industry FICO scale (up to 900); none are outside 250-900.

subvented as written, with repeated <subvented> elements joined by a comma: 2024-A '0' 3,955, '1' 41,608, '1,2' 18,922, '2' 2,108; 2025-A '0' 1,838, '1' 16,114, '1,2' 46,513, '2' 499; 2025-B '1,2' 42,428, '2' 10,105 (no '0' at all). Spec codes: 0 No, 1 Rate subvention, 2 Cash rebate, 98 Other. apr_pct is exactly 0 for 10,508 / 6,546 / 3,699 loans; maximum 11.99 in all three (424B5 range 0.00% to 11.99%).

Pools are seasoned: origination months 2018-03..2024-01 (cutoff 2024-04), 2019-04..2024-11 (cutoff 2025-04), 2019-10..2025-06 (cutoff 2025-10). Share originated 12 or more months before the cutoff month: 45.4% / 49.2% / 60.9%. No loan was originated after 2026-01.

Other codes as written: interest_rate_type_code '1' (fixed) for every loan; vehicle_type_code '98' (other) for most loans (38,454 / 35,013 / 31,627) plus 1/2/3; vehicle_value_source_code '1' (invoice) for exactly the new-vehicle loans, '3' or '98' otherwise; income_verification_code and employment_verification_code '2' for every loan; asset numbers carry a letter suffix (e.g. '16455700b'). vehicle_make is upper case ('NISSAN', 'INFINITI').

Downloads: Python requests (one curl call for the earlier 2025-B lp file) with the sec.gov User-Agent from CLAUDE.md passed in the SEC_UA environment variable (not stored in any file), one request at a time, at least 1.1 s apart, no retries; every request is logged in data/raw/nissan/sec_requests.log (git-ignored). The earlier 2025-B lp file was meant to be a 640 KB range request; SEC ignored the Range header and sent all 186,757,595 bytes (HTTP 200), which made the full comparison possible; that copy was deleted afterwards.
couldnt_confirm: The sp/mp pool files and the original 2025-A lp file (superseded by the amendment) were not downloaded, so their loan counts were not checked; the lp choice rests on the exact match of row count and balance with the 424B5.

Filing dates of Nissan 2023-B and 2024-B were not checked; 2024-A (first filing 2024-05-07) is taken as the only Nissan receivables deal with a pool filing in Jan-Jun 2024 because 2023-B carries a 2023 name and 2024-B is the next deal after 2024-A.
What 999.99 in paymentToIncomePercentage and vehicle_type_code '98' mean in Nissan's practice, and why 2025-B has no loan with subvented '0' (Nissan's EX-103 explanatory notes were not opened).
